text: Hey class! I'm Beeswax, your unbeelievably charming and handsome bee assistant.
Bees are super important for our planet. Six things around you matter a lot to bees.
Walk up to one and look at it. Got a question? I'll always BEE here, so interrupt me anytime!
Bee fact found! Would you like to learn more?
I'll take that as a yes.
Don't worry, I'll BEE right here if you need anything.

label: native_flower
text: This is a sunflower. It grew wild in North America first.

label: native_flower
text: Some scientists think one in three bites you eat is thanks to pollinators like me.

label: native_flower
text: Your next adventure: the sunflower. Go find it.

label: honey_jar
text: This is honey. One pound can take up to two million flower visits.

label: honey_jar
text: Never leave store honey out for bees. It can carry a bee germ called foulbrood. Still fine on your toast.

label: honey_jar
text: Now go to your next adventure. One big step to your left.

label: bug_spray
text: This is bug spray. Bees carry it home to the babies.

label: bug_spray
text: One study: US farmland got about forty-eight times more toxic for insects to eat in twenty-two years.

label: bug_spray
text: Next adventure: one more step to your left. Brace yourself.

label: bee_hotel
text: This is a bee hotel, a safe home for wild bees like mason bees.

label: bee_hotel
text: Nearly one in four kinds of wild bees scientists checked is in danger. Bee hotels help them hang on.

label: bee_hotel
text: Ugh. Get away from that can. Your next adventure is one step to your left.

label: pebble_dish
text: This is a bee water dish. Bees can't swim, so pebbles are their landing pads.

label: pebble_dish
text: On a hot day, bees haul home about eighty percent of their weight in water to cool the hive.

label: pebble_dish
text: Thirsty? Your next adventure is one step to your left.

label: beehive
text: This is a beehive. Last year, US beekeepers lost about four in ten of their hives.

label: beehive
text: The year before, more than half: the worst on record. Tiny mites spreading bee viruses are a big reason.

label: beehive
text: Last adventure. One step to your left. It's the big one.
You found them all! Bee Scout badge earned!
Now you know: flowers feed us, honey takes millions of flower visits, and bug spray hurts bees.
Give bees a home and a drink, and help save the hives. BEE-autiful work, scout!
A little to your left.
A little to your right.
Closer. Bees are small. So are my eyes.
Lift your chin a little so I can see it.
Hey! Where'd you go? I'm a bee, not a bloodhound. Find the next picture.
Ask your teacher for another assignment!
